acceptance: Fake-clock tests cover primary/secondary limits, transient 5xx and budget exhaustion across trunk/review/tracker reads; unreadable state never arms.
pr-open reports actual lookup/rate-limit cause and reset/retry guidance, not a misleading review-unavailable result.
Permanent auth/permission errors fail promptly; recovered waits re-read current head/gates and stay within WAIT.

A network timeout (for example a TLS handshake timeout) or an unparseable tracker read inside the WAIT budget is retried with bounded backoff; the outcome line names the transient cause when the budget runs out
No path arms on an unreadable trunk, review-gate or tracker state (asserted by a test for each transient kind)

description:
Gap seen three times on 2026-11-12 (PR #4169 twice, PR #4175 once). While waiting, `pr-arm` calls `gh run list` for the trunk check; when the account's REST quota is exhausted (several agent sessions share one user) it prints `trunk-arm-gate: refusing: gh run list failed: HTTP 403: API rate limit exceeded` and exits non-zero with most of the `WAIT` budget unused. The reset time is known (`gh api rate_limit` does not count against the quota) and was 3 minutes away in the first case. Each caller then has to notice, compute the reset and start again, which is the hand-written loop the guide forbids.

Expected: within the `WAIT` budget, a 403 rate-limit response is treated as waiting, not refusal: sleep until the reported reset (bounded by the remaining budget), then continue. Outside the budget, exit with an outcome that names the reset time.

Guardrails: never treat an unreadable trunk state as passing; arming still requires a successful read. No retry on other 4xx responses. `scripts/pr_arm.py` and `scripts/trunk_revert.py` currently contain no rate-limit handling.

## Decision gates
Preserve the merged duplicate scope: pr-open lookup failures, pr-arm tracker/trunk/review reads, 403/429 reset and Retry-After, plus transient 5xx. Implementer chooses bounded backoff within WAIT; owner approval is required for any gate-policy change.

## Verification rubric
Pass: deterministic fake-clock tests cover reset within and beyond WAIT, secondary limit, 503 recovery/exhaustion, permanent permission denial and a moved head while waiting. No unreadable state arms. pr-open names reset/retry cause rather than reporting unavailable review; successful recovery re-evaluates current head and every gate.

## Additional guardrails
No busy polling, quota-exhaustion experiments, blanket retries of 4xx, extra publication or new wait loops outside repository entry points. Preserve rate-volume reduction delivered separately.
